job.cancel.what: stop a long operation where whoever started it left a way to, and say so by name where it did not, rather than leaving somebody watching a bar that carries on

params.name: id
params.what: the job's id, as job.list reports it; an id no running job carries is refused, and so is one whose job cannot be interrupted safely - job.list's `cancellable` says which before it is pressed

job.cancel.answers: The row stays on the list with "stopping" put in front of what it says, because the work ends when its context notices, which is not this instant, and a row that vanished on the press would be claiming otherwise.

job.done.what: take a job off the list, because a progress bar that never goes away is a worse lie than no progress bar
job.done.answers: Nothing, and an id no job carries is not an error: the work finishing twice is commoner than the row being missing.

job.progress.what: create or move on one row of the job list, carrying forward the cancel function of the row it replaces
job.progress.answers: Nothing. It carries a state.Job, a Go value holding a closure nothing outside the process can spell, so anything else is refused.
